notes: GPUI PANEL. The target UI framework is GPUI 0.2.2 (Zed's framework), not React. You have no training knowledge of this exact API, so read before writing: rever/src/main.rs (the app shell: how views, listeners, canvas, hover, scrolling, text fields and theme are used here), every file in rever-ui-kit/src (theme tokens, icons, strings via `Lang::t`, the TextInput entity, preview::run), vendor/gpui/examples/*.rs (uniform_list.rs, scrollable.rs, data_table.rs, input.rs are the most relevant) and vendor/gpui/src/elements/*.rs for exact method names. What to build: a view struct that implements gpui::Render and reproduces the React component's layout, sizes, colors and behaviors (filters, selection, the detail drawer with its tabs, the JSON tree with expand/collapse). Colors and sizes come from src/renderer/src/styles.css tokens (already in rever_ui_kit::theme::Theme; if a token you need is missing, define it locally in your crate and list it in your report). Data: the React code reads traffic over IPC and a zustand store; here the view takes `Arc<Mutex<rever_core::traffic::TrafficStore>>` and reads it on render, with a `refresh` method the host calls when new traffic arrives. All user-facing strings go through `rever_ui_kit::i18n::Lang::t(key)` with the same keys the TSX uses (keys the TSX hardcodes in English stay English literals). Keep logic (filtering, sorting, formatting, JSON tree flattening) in plain functions with Korean-named unit tests; a .tsx file counts as ported (and gets the `Port of` marker) only when its behaviors are all there. Large lists must use gpui's uniform_list so 500 rows stay fast. Preview: fill examples/preview.rs so that `cargo run -p rever-ui-traffic --example preview_traffic` shows the view with realistic fixture data (use rever_ui_kit::preview::run; the window is unfocused and closes itself after REVER_PREVIEW_SECONDS, default 6). Look at your own work: while the preview runs, `scripts/capture-window.sh preview_traffic /tmp/preview_traffic.png` captures only that window; read the PNG and compare it with what the TSX would render, then fix what is off. Do not bring windows to the front, do not capture the screen any other way, and do not run the `rever` app. The first build of a GPUI crate takes a few minutes.
